components.html:
In this article
  • What the official count measures
  • Sources

In this article

  • What the official count measures
  • Sources

In brief

  • Marriage registrations do not measure wedding vendor revenue.
  • Survey averages describe respondents, not every Australian wedding.
  • Check external research against your own bookings and delivery costs.

Australia recorded 118,804 registered marriages in 2025, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics release published on 28 July 2026. That was 1.7% fewer than in 2024. It is the latest complete national annual release available at the time of writing, not a count of weddings held so far in 2026. [1]

What the official count measures

The ABS collects administrative marriage records from state and territory registries. Its scope includes overseas visitors who marry here and excludes Australian residents who marry overseas. Registration and reporting delays also mean the reference year can differ from the year a ceremony happened. [2]

Sources

    Marriages and Divorces, Australia, 2025

    Australian Bureau of Statistics

  2. 2
    Marriages and Divorces, Australia methodology, 2025

    Australian Bureau of Statistics

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Ruled Sheet"**

The site is one printed run sheet, nav to footer, set in the console's own register. Every section is a full-bleed row whose top rule crosses the window; inside it the sheet is a single column whose two side rules run unbroken from the top of the window to the foot of the page, with a small ink registration cross wherever a row rule meets a column rule. Cells butt against each other inside that column and draw their own hairlines, so a claim always sits in a cell beside the real console screen that proves it.

The register is the software's, deliberately. White page, grey-green Panel cells, near-black Ink, Bottle for structure and one lit Sprout action per view. Corners are 6px, buttons carry a letterpress bottom edge, and only floating chrome casts a shadow. A visitor should finish the page thinking "that is my console", because the tokens here are the console kit's own (arbour/packages/ui/src/styles/globals.css) and the site only adds what a long marketing page needs: fluid display steps, the ruled sheet, the stage strip and the capture frame.

The world refuses the feature-card grid and the retired marketing look (Acid, Cream floods, square corners, the Acid stage rail). Colour arrives in whole rows or cells, never as tinted cards on white.
keyCharacteristics: One continuous ruled column, 1280px maximum, with registration marks at every crossing.
White by default; Panel for sunken cells; Bottle only for the close.
Bricolage 800 hard left at fluid sizes, with optical size doing the tightening.
Martian Mono as a small uppercase label voice: captions, field labels, indices, block heads.
Real screens as proof, with claims that point at measured regions of them.
6px corners, letterpress depth on content, blur only on floating chrome.

rules.name: The One Lit Action Rule
rules.body: Sprout marks the single thing to do next in any view: the trial button. Every other button is Bottle, secondary or ghost. Two Sprout buttons in one view means there is no headline action.

rules.name: The Status Is Not Decoration Rule
rules.body: Coral and Ochre speak only for danger and warning. Category leaves use Bottle, Sprout, Cornflower and Lilac only.

rules.name: The Bottle Close Rule
rules.body: The Bottle band is reserved for the close: the final call to action and the footer under it. Inside a Bottle band the rules turn On Dark at 14%, the marks On Dark at 60%, and the focus ring Sprout at 70%.

rules.name: The One Panel Band Rule
rules.body: Pricing is the one full Panel band on the home page. Elsewhere Panel lives in cells, not rows.

rules.name: The No Acid, No Cream Rule
rules.body: Acid and Cream are print and social colours. Neither appears on a screen; Acid survives only as the A on the app icon.

rules.name: The Eight Hundred Rule
rules.body: Bricolage is set at 800 and nothing else, with no added letter spacing and balanced wrapping. The `opsz` axis does the tightening.

rules.name: The Label Voice Rule
rules.body: Mono is always uppercase and always small. It captions, labels fields, indexes and heads the console's blocks. It never sits above a heading as a kicker and never carries a sentence of body copy.

rules.name: The Numbers Are Display Rule
rules.body: Prices, counts and stage numbers are Bricolage 800, never body.

rules.name: The Lift Is For Chrome Rule
rules.body: A blurred shadow means the object floats over the page. Content cells, captures and plan cells never cast one; they sit in the sheet.

rules.name: The Lift On Hover Rule
rules.body: Solid buttons rise 3px on the overshoot curve, with a 6px hover bridge under them so the cursor never drops off mid-lift, and settle back on press.

dos: Do put every new section in a ruled row inside the sheet, so the column rules and registration marks stay continuous from nav to footer.
Do set a claim in a cell beside the real screen that proves it, and give it measured regions when the screen can show it.
Do keep one Sprout action per view; make every other button Bottle, secondary or ghost.
Do set headlines in Bricolage 800 hard left with no added tracking, using the fluid steps (stage, headline, readout, hero, statement).
Do use mono labels to caption, to label fields, to index and to head a console block.
Do use 6px corners, 4px for small controls, 2px for leaves.
Do use the 3px Bottle 55% focus outline on white and the Sprout 70% outline on Bottle.

Do let motion pop on the overshoot (`cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.8, 0.45, 1)`, 260ms) and slide on the glide (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 0.84, 0.36, 1)`, 180 to 320ms), and keep content visible when motion is reduced.
donts: Don't build a feature-card grid or flood a mid-page section with colour; the Bottle band is the close and Pricing is the one Panel band.
Don't put Acid or Cream on a screen.
Don't use Coral or Ochre for anything but danger and warning.
Don't set a mono kicker or eyebrow above a heading.
Don't cast a blurred shadow from content; only floating chrome lifts.
Don't use a radius above 6px, a pill, a gradient or glassmorphism.
Don't use a grey hex for a border; borders are translucent Ink and rules are Line.
Don't put Sprout in the Arby Help panel.
